summary: The bill amends 10 U.S.C. § 130i to expand Defense Department authority to detect and neutralize unmanned aircraft threats to more facilities and scenarios, delegate that power to combatant commanders and service secretaries, allow support to other agencies, exempt related information from disclosure, and extend reporting deadlines to 2030.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends authorities under title 10 for DoD and Coast Guard counter-drone operations but contains no appropriations, funding authorizations, or spending directives. Any future implementation costs are indirect and unspecified.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
The legislation is exclusively focused on unmanned aircraft threat mitigation and has no connection to healthcare policy or systems.
No references to firearms, ammunition, or gun regulations appear in the bill.
The bill does not address immigration, border policy, visas, or related enforcement.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the bill expands DoD authorities for counter-UAS operations, it does not alter funding levels, budgets, or spending authorizations for defense.
No environmental regulations, protections, or climate-related measures are included.
The bill contains nothing related to welfare programs, entitlements, or social assistance.
No education policy, school funding, or curriculum provisions exist in the text.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance measures are present.

The bill carves out limited exemptions from certain title 18 provisions for authorized DoD/Coast Guard counter-drone activities, but this is narrowly tailored to national-security operations rather than broader criminal-justice policy.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export rules are addressed.
The legislation does not affect deficit levels, debt ceilings, or fiscal-balance requirements.
No provisions touch on LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
Foreign assistance programs are not mentioned.
The bill has no bearing on voting access, election administration, or campaign rules.

Section 2(5) adds an explicit FOIA exemption (5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3)) for counter-UAS technology, procedures, and protocols, thereby reducing public disclosure and oversight of these systems. This constitutes a minor, tangential reduction in transparency requirements.
No labor, union, or workplace-protection provisions are present.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
